items.title: Apple cracks the door open to Siri AI
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,926 new readers. Years of Apple Intelligence and one full Siri rebuild later, the iPhone still doesn’t feel any more like a device built for the AI era. Could letting other apps in finally change that?

Apple just opened up building on its Siri AI to all developers, something the notoriously closed-off ecosystem rarely allows. But none of it reaches the App Store until spring, which could be a whole different AI era for a product already feeling generations behind.

Founders and solo operators: You’re doing the work of a whole team by yourself — show us how AI makes that possible. Outreach, invoicing, content, customer replies, anything counts. Submit your workflow for a chance to be featured in the newsletter.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Apple lets any app plug into Siri AI

  • Google won’t give schools Search without AI

  • Turn one product photo into three studio shots

  • CrowdStrike’s ‘kill switch’ to stop rogue AI agents

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

APPLE

🍎 Apple lets any app plug into Siri AI

Image source: Apple

The Rundown: Apple just released a developer preview of Siri AI in its latest software betas, giving apps of any kind a way to build their own features into the assistant — though developers can only test it for now, and customers are still months away.

The details:

  • Siri AI is Apple’s rebuilt assistant, able to see a user’s screen and read messages, and has been a waitlisted beta since iOS 27 shipped in September.

  • Developers can now add their own actions instead of just Apple’s initial preset list of options, and teach Siri multi-step jobs through new “skills.”

  • For now, app versions stay with a developer’s internal testers, App Store submissions start in spring, and Apple says rules for developers will come later.

  • The betas also bring China its first Apple Intelligence tools (minus Siri AI) and test new Apple Watch tools that listen in the background to transcribe nearby talk.

Why it matters: Apple letting any app build into Siri is a real crack in its walled garden, which is a big deal. Still, it leaves the work on developers, and between Siri AI’s confusing rollout and the progress other frontier labs have made in areas like computer use, the best AI features still feel a long way off for the world’s most popular phone.

TOGETHER WITH WIZ

🔒 Securing AI Agents 101

The Rundown: AI agents are rapidly emerging across enterprise environments: powering automation, chaining tools, and acting across systems. Securing AI Agents 101 is a one-page resource to help teams build a clear understanding of what AI agents are, how they operate, and where key security considerations show up.

Inside, you’ll find:

  • What makes an AI agent different from traditional tools

  • Top risks to watch, from shadow AI to excessive permissions

  • Four key questions to assess agent usage and exposure

Get the one-page guide to AI agents.

GOOGLE & AI IN SCHOOLS

🏫 Google won’t give schools Search without AI

Image source: Google

The Rundown: Google announced that K-12 student accounts will start with Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook all off early next year, potentially forcing districts that want AI out of classrooms to also give up Google Search for their students.

The details:

  • Education VP Chris Phillips said to The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” and students at AI-free schools will see a notice that it’s off.

  • NYC and LA, the two largest U.S. districts, restricted AI for ~1M students this semester, and Fairfax County, VA, built a plugin to hide Google’s AI summaries.

  • Google’s announcement also comes one day after the Nov. 2 deadline senators gave the company to answer questions about pushing AI into schools.

  • Ex-FTC Chair Lina Khan said Google is using “its search monopoly to coerce schools” and will “punish those who don’t fall in line.”

  • Google later defended the move on X as “more choice, not less,” but its post only describes Search with AI Mode and AI Overviews, never without them.

Why it matters: Google is essentially saying out loud what the trend has shown — Google Search is AI search now — and schools aren’t getting the old version back. The stranger situation will be AI-free districts with kids on Chromebooks, turning in work through Classroom, and writing in Docs, yet unable to use Search.

AI TRAINING

📷 Turn one product photo into three studio shots

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll build a product-shoot app in Runway using an image of a vintage Polaroid camera. You’ll create coral, sunlit, and blue-lit scenes, then save the app so you can repeat the process.

Step-by-step:

  1. Save the guide’s Polaroid photo and its credit. Open Runway App Studio and check that your plan and credit balance support a build

  2. Paste the build prompt to create an app with three shoot presets. Check the product upload, scene menu, and download controls before running it

  3. Upload the original photo and list the camera details to preserve. Make one coral studio shot and inspect the lens, rainbow stripe, buttons, and lettering

  4. Run the same photo through the sunlit and blue-lit presets. Keep the camera’s shape and viewpoint consistent, and save each approved result

  5. Publish the app for yourself, then open all three downloads. Keep the source credit and a record of any defects with the set

Pro tip: Use the original product photo for every scene. Starting from a flawed AI image can carry its mistakes into the next shot. Visit The Rundown University to get the full guide, materials, files, and more.

PRESENTED BY PITCH

📣 Teams riding the AI wave present with Pitch

The Rundown: The teams building AI make their slides with Pitch. It’s how Perplexity, fal, Legora, Poolside, and Synthesia create and deliver presentations at scale.

Pitch is an agentic presentation platform where you can:

  • Generate fully editable decks from your own templates, so every slide stays on brand

  • Connect via MCP to personalize slides with data from your CRM or call notes

  • Nurture deals with custom pitch rooms, and track how buyers engage with built-in analytics

Try Pitch.

CROWDSTRIKE & AI SECURITY

🛑 CrowdStrike’s ‘kill switch’ to stop rogue AI agents

Image source: CrowdStrike

The Rundown: Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike unveiled the AI Kill Switch, adding an emergency stop to its Falcon Guardian security platform for businesses worried about their AI agents going rogue.

The details:

  • The switch targets an agent’s link to its AI model, not the model itself, while Falcon Guardian separately monitors tools like Claude Code and Codex.

  • A human admin has to pull the trigger, and every use gets logged, while shutting agents down directly on work devices and in the cloud is “coming soon.”

  • CEO George Kurtz explained it like a race car’s brake, saying it sits outside the AI so an agent “can’t argue with it, rewrite it, or wait it out.”

  • CrowdStrike is also buying monitoring firm Fiddler AI and security tester Dreadnode for a reported $495M, and added Claude Cowork protection in beta.

Why it matters: Politicians have spent the summer fighting over an AI kill switch, with a pair of bills and a California executive order aimed at rogue AI agents. CrowdStrike is bringing the same concept to enterprises… where the likelier scenario isn’t a frontier model escaping a lab, but an agent holding the company’s logins going off script.

▸ Erin built a self-drafting timesheet with Claude

Today’s workflow comes from reader Erin Reid:

“Late timesheets delayed accurate client billing for our advertising and marketing agency, so I built a Claude project that reconstructs my week from the tools I already use. It drafts time entries that I review and approve before anything reaches our system. It’s useful for anyone who logs time after the fact and loses track of smaller tasks.

It searches the emails I sent or replied to, my calendar meetings, files I edited in Google Drive, Slack threads I joined, work-related browsing, and Claude work sessions. It builds a daily timeline and groups related items into one block. An email, a doc edit, and a Slack thread about the same issue count once.

The project instructions require Claude never to invent work or pad hours, never to double-count, and to disclose any source it couldn’t search. Instead of trying to remember my week, I now review entries that already have project codes and descriptions, and it also surfaces work I had forgotten.”

items.title: MIT shows AI improving AI, no training required
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,563 new readers. Every few weeks, it seems another leading AI lab says that an autonomous AI researcher is closer to reality. New MIT research just gave a peek at how much of that capability may be sitting inside models already available to the public.

GPT-6 Astra went inside a smaller AI with poor math scores and improved it directly, skipping the training that normally does that work. Once improving a model is as simple as pointing another one at it, AI’s already frantic pace could hit another gear.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • OpenAI’s Astra rewrites other AI from the inside

  • OpenAI grades its AI on everyday tasks

  • Turn one interview into two clips with Riverside

  • OpenAI joins Abu Dhabi’s AI-native government push

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

AI RESEARCH

🔬 OpenAI’s Astra rewrites other AI from the inside

Image source: MIT CSAIL

The Rundown: MIT researchers just published research showing that OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra can improve some AI models by directly rewriting their weights — the numbers that decide how a model behaves — rather than putting them through more training.

The details:

  • Weights are normally set through training, since even small AI models have far too many to read or adjust by hand.

  • Alibaba’s small Qwen model scored 7.9% in math until Astra changed just 0.016% of those weights to cut its habit of repeating itself, hitting 48.1% after the fix.

  • The same approach did little for Google’s smaller Gemma 3, which lacked a single flaw like Qwen’s repetition, barely moving its math score.

  • Smaller tests also had Astra name the game an AI had learned from its weights alone, and write a simple Breakout player from scratch without training.

  • The authors say this capability could one day let AI upgrade itself, add or remove skills in other models on request, or check them for hidden problems.

Why it matters: The top AI labs are racing toward self-improving, automated AI researchers, and while this research is just one small example, it may be a sign of where things are headed. Once models are strong enough to alter and improve their weights, we’re in major “takeoff” territory, where AI starts speeding up its own progress.

TOGETHER WITH OPTIMIZELY

🔎 Finding AI use cases in your workflows

The Rundown: When it comes to AI planning, the highest-value use cases are already living inside your workflows — you just have to know where to look. Optimizely’s template helps you find AI use cases that really matter in just a few minutes.

The template gives you:

  • A 3-step framework to build the foundation of your next AI agent

  • The exact process that turned a 2-3 hour GA4 reporting task into a 5-minute one

  • Real use cases mapped to how your team actually works

Download the template for better AI use cases.

OPENAI

📋 OpenAI grades its AI on everyday tasks

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just introduced LifeVal, a new test grading how well AI gets through everyday errands like booking appointments, buying groceries, and filling out government forms, with tasks chosen based on what people say they want help with.

The details:

  • The selected task areas come from a poll of 4K people on where they want help, and global time-use surveys on what everyday tasks consume time.

  • LifeVal has been OpenAI’s internal measurement for the past year, as it trained models to browse the web, operate a computer, and work in connected apps.

  • OpenAI’s models have gone from an average score of 49.3% (GPT-5.2) to 80.6% (GPT-6 Astra), though just 0.6 points of that gain came after July’s GPT-5.6.

  • Astra’s “best recorded” scores hit 100% on 10 of 16 tasks OpenAI listed, like replacing a lost engagement ring, with LSAT help scoring the lowest at 88.7%.

Why it matters: We look at benchmark results on everything from coding and math to business tasks, but few have measured how models handle the everyday tasks that a more general audience is asking AI to do. Seeing this eval tested across other models would be an interesting data point for the personal agent meta seen across the industry.

AI TRAINING

🎬 Turn one interview into two clips with Riverside

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use Riverside’s new agents to turn a licensed interview into two captioned videos. You’ll choose useful moments, check the edits, and prepare post drafts without filming anything new.

Step-by-step:

  1. Download the guide’s openly licensed interview and save its credit. Then, make an MP4 copy and upload it to a Riverside practice project

  2. Ask Clipper for short passages that make sense on their own. Make sure to watch the surrounding interview before choosing your two clips

  3. Ask Editor for a matching vertical layout, keeping the full picture visible and leaving space for captions and the source label

  4. Check the captions against the speech, then ask Marketer for two short post drafts. Keep the interview’s date and full credit with each one

  5. Finally, export both clips and watch the saved files. Check the framing, sound, words, and ending before handing them off

Pro tip: A shorter clip can change what someone seems to mean. Keep the question or qualifying sentence when the answer depends on it. Visit The Rundown University to get the full guide, materials, files, and more.

PRESENTED BY PAVE

🔧 The simple fix for apps that stall

The Rundown: Vibe coding makes building apps fast. But it’s also left piles of slick-looking apps that sit unused because they can’t talk to the tools you rely on every day. Pave gives you the speed without the dead end.

With Pave, you can:

  • Describe your process and get a working custom app in minutes

  • Link to 350+ systems, including Quickbase, on every plan

  • Create workflows to run reminders, approvals, and handoffs on their own

Build now.

AI & THE WORLD

🤝 OpenAI joins Abu Dhabi’s AI-native government push

Image source: Abu Dhabi Media Office

The Rundown: OpenAI just sealed four agreements in Abu Dhabi, bringing its AI to state oil giant ADNOC, the emirate’s government, and state investor Mubadala, while a UAE group is reportedly set to be the top investor in the AI giant’s raise of up to $20B.

The details:

  • ADNOC’s deal, the largest of the four, aims to cut oil field planning from months to hours by running decades of well data through OpenAI’s models.

  • Food imports come first in “Machine-Readable Government,” a project turning some Abu Dhabi rules into text AI can read to help streamline permit processes.

  • Abu Dhabi already has a $3.5B plan for AI across all public services, and a separate OpenAI and Microsoft program aims to train 20K staff and the public.

  • OpenAI’s models will help Mubadala weigh risk and spot new bets, while a five-year pact with AI firm G42’s Inception42 targets UAE businesses and schools.

Why it matters: Albania gained headlines last year by naming a digital AI “minister,” but Abu Dhabi’s version is more practical — giving AI better access to existing data and rules to improve efficiency. The circular AI dealmaking also continues, with Abu Dhabi acting as both a major deployer of OpenAI’s tech and potentially the biggest investor.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Judd built an AI research team that fact-checks itself

Today’s workflow comes from reader Judd Slivka:

“I use a four-step system built on Grok Bot to get AI-generated research reports with fewer errors. It’s for anyone who relies on AI research and needs to trust the numbers and quotes in it.

I start with a research bot that has specific instructions. They cover the types of sources it should use, separating known facts from speculative claims, and cross-checking claims. The report goes to a skeptic. The skeptic is meant to be contrarian but not a roadblock. It asks for evidence, looks for logical fallacies, and creates a short, ranked list of problems. The problem list goes back to the researcher, who then passes the report to my fact-checker. The fact-checker double-checks every number and every quote or paraphrase against the actual document it was found in.

The result is a report with fewer errors, but also flags on what’s verified and what isn’t. Far and away the most valuable workflow that I’ve built. It costs more in terms of usage, but it’s been working great.”

  • 🗣️ Decision Model API - Hume’s AI that answers queries about voice recordings

items.title: AI backlash heads to the polls
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 8,118 new readers. AI spent the last two years winning over Washington. This week, it faces a tougher crowd: voters ready to hit the polls and evict the buildout from their own backyards.

With data centers now a defining midterm issue, OpenAI already floating a new name for them, and control of the House up for grabs, AI’s next wave of construction could get a lot harder — no matter what the industry decides to call it.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Data centers hit the ballot as OpenAI plots a rebrand

  • The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

  • Make AI artwork you can actually edit

  • Google’s space data center sends home a haiku

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

AI & POLITICS

🗳️ Data centers hit the ballot as OpenAI plots a rebrand

Image source: Wikimedia Commons

The Rundown: This week’s U.S. midterms double as a referendum on data centers, with roughly 20 communities voting on bans or pauses, while OpenAI reportedly prepares a post-election push to rebrand the sites as “AI compute campuses.”

The details:

  • Democrats are projected to flip the House Tuesday, which could end a two-year run of easy treatment in Washington for AI firms with close ties to Pres. Trump.

  • Some Democrats want a federal freeze on new data centers, including House hopefuls Will Lawrence in Michigan and Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin.

  • The White House already got tech giants to voluntarily supply their own power, and last week Trump floated having developers pay locals a “dividend” as well.

  • OpenAI is planning to pitch the campuses as local economic boosts, citing a Pike County, Ohio, project it’s helping build that promises thousands of jobs.

  • OpenAI policy chief Chris Lehane called the debate “democracy in action,” and the company wants state bills giving locals a voice in new projects.

Why it matters: AI has a real image problem with the public, and data centers have become one of the defining fights of Tuesday’s elections. That anger won’t be fixed by a new name or a few community perks, and a Democratic House could make life a lot harder for AI giants trying to scale their infrastructure bets against local opposition.

TOGETHER WITH GARTNER

📓 Is your AI strategy ready for what’s next? 

The Rundown: 42% of enterprises plan to deploy AI agents by the end of 2026, but only 22% capture significant value today. The Gartner Top Tech Trends for 2027 reveal how enterprises can shift into the autonomous era and get ahead.

Key themes include:

  • Leveraging the nontextual AI frontier

  • Governing the autonomous agent platform

  • Architecting durable agility

Explore the trends.

THE RUNDOWN ROUNDTABLE

💡 The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

The Rundown: The Rundown Roundtable is a weekly feature where we poll members of The Rundown staff about how we use AI in our work and daily lives.

Nick, Video Producer: When I create video content, I pull imagery from many different sources, so my editing folder often ends up with photos that may or may not work inside my editing program. For a handful of photos, converting them manually is fine. For larger projects with dozens of images, it eats into my time and focus. I wanted something simple, lightweight on compute power, that could batch convert photos.

I asked Claude to create an app that runs on my local machine and can batch convert photos into formats I know will work in my video editor.

Claude returned an app that worked exactly the way I needed. I asked Claude to install it on my computer, and it was working within seconds. I now use the app to batch convert my photo folders before bringing them into the editor.

There are plenty of traditional ways to do this, but with Claude I got a solution that fit my workflow perfectly, and large image batches no longer slow my editing down.

Shubham, Editor: I had about $2K in contributions from past jobs stuck in a government scheme for more than two years. The portal was slow, spread across several forms, and unclear about how to withdraw the money.

I gave the task to Claude and Perplexity Comet. Claude worked through the rules and found the withdrawal route that kept my tax bill lowest. Comet then verified and implemented that route. It ran the portal in my browser, filled in and submitted the claim forms, and let me watch the screen and check each detail before submission. Two weeks later, the $2K arrived.

After that, Claude compared the amount I received with the scheme’s online statement and found a gap: interest that had not been paid out. It filed a second form for the difference, and I’m waiting for the payment now. I’ll use the same technique to solve this for my wife, too.

AI TRAINING

🎨 Make AI artwork you can actually edit

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use Arrow 2 to create a three-part graphic for a client proposal. You’ll refine one scene, add editable headings, and change a color without generating the artwork again.

Step-by-step:

  1. Open QuiverAI, select Arrow 2, and check that your plan includes SVG export. Install Inkscape for the final text and color changes

  2. Paste the guide’s brief to draw a folder, review board, and laptop in one matching style. Leave space for the title and headings

  3. Ask Arrow to replace one badge with speech bubbles. Compare the result with the original and check that the other scenes stay intact

  4. Download the SVG and open it in Inkscape. Add the headings, then change the middle label and one screen color directly

  5. Save the editable master and export a high-resolution PNG. Reopen both files and check the words, colors, and dimensions before sharing

Pro tip: Keep text that may change in separate text boxes. You can fix a heading or update a client’s wording without spending another generation on the artwork. Visit The Rundown University to get the full guide, materials, files, and more.

PRESENTED BY CONDUCTOR

🔎 Discover your brand’s top AEO priority

The Rundown: Trade chance for certainty with Conductor’s free AEO Analysis. Compare your mentions with competitors, see which content gets cited, understand funnel visibility, and identify opportunities. 500+ brands are already winning AI search with Conductor.

The free report analyzes:

  • AI market share showing your brand mentions vs. competitors

  • Funnel visibility with top prompts by search intent

  • Content performance based on total AI citations

  • Brand sentiment revealing how AI perceives your brand

Get your free AEO analysis.

AI, DATACENTERS, & SPACE

🛰️ Google’s space data center sends home a haiku

Image source: Google / SpaceX

The Rundown: Google just announced that its Project Suncatcher satellite answered its first AI prompt from orbit, with Google’s open Gemma 4 model writing a haiku in an early test of the company’s moonshot goal to put AI data centers in space.

The details:

  • Gemma’s haiku (Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core) reached the ground while the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway.

  • Google CEO Sundar Pichai called it “a ‘hello world’ milestone,” a reference to the test programmers typically run first on a new machine.

  • Power is still a big constraint, with the craft able to run just one of its four Google AI chips (TPUs), and only in bursts of roughly 20 minutes.

  • Two more powerful satellites launching in 2027 will test the laser links a fleet needs to split one AI job, if the chips first survive radiation and heat tests.

Why it matters: An admittedly heartwarming haiku still won’t win over a public that is increasingly fed up with data centers of any kind, but moving them to orbit could eventually be a compromise that sidesteps a lot of the issues driving that anger — making this moonshot project a big one to keep an eye on.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ John built an AI ops team for his photography business

Today’s workflow comes from reader John Fertic:

“I run a photography business and built a three-layer AI workflow to help with daily operations, business improvement, and watching for outside changes that might affect us. It's for small business owners who don't want to monitor every source or handle every issue themselves.

The layers are an Operations Core (dashboard, estimates, schedules, reminders, project records, and other business state), a Work orchestrator with specialist AI agents, and a signal and triage system that watches platform alerts, vendor updates, local-search changes, newsletters, calendars, and marketing sources.

Work decides whether a signal actually matters and routes it to the right specialist. The WordPress and Google Business Profile specialists are connected directly to those systems through MCP/API connectors, so they can compare the incoming signal against the current state of the actual site or profile. The system brings me in only when a real decision is needed. The main benefit for me is that I don't have to personally track every source or jump into every issue.”

  • 🗣️ Phonic-1 - SOTA voice model that swaps between 50+ languages mid-call

  • 🐳 Super-Agent - DeepSeek’s prototype open-source coding agent

  • 🖼️ Brush - Canva’s new vision-language model that edits designs via text

*Sponsored Listing

📰 Everything else in AI today

Atlassian’s webinar on the State of the Developer Experience in 2026 features insights from industry experts on moving beyond AI adoption to operationalization. Register today.*

Cisco president Jeetu Patel revealed that he put a 27-year-old ex-founder who was “buried away in the organization doing something unstrategic” in charge of trying to rewrite the company’s legacy code, giving him unlimited tokens and orders to “go nuts.”

items.content:

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,617 new readers. Nvidia’s chips are at the center of the U.S.-China AI race, and Washington has spent years trying to keep the best ones out of Beijing’s hands.

Now, a New York Times report says U.S. intelligence found that an alleged Chinese asset had built close ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang… and the White House chose not to act.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Report: Nvidia CEO targeted by alleged Chinese spy

  • Rowan’s Corner: ‘Sent from my agent’

  • Make ElevenLabs voiceovers sound more natural

  • Anthropic’s AI now monitors its own conversations

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

NVIDIA

🕵️ Report: Nvidia CEO targeted by alleged Chinese spy

Image source: Net Thunder on LinkedIn

The Rundown: The NYT just reported that U.S. officials found Alice Huang, an exec at Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed, was allegedly passing intelligence to Beijing while keeping close ties with Jensen Huang, with Trump briefed about a year ago.

The details:

  • It’s unclear what Ms. Huang passed to Beijing or its value, but officials worried she could offer insight into Trump’s view on chip sales to China, and into Nvidia itself.

  • Officials didn’t believe Jensen knew of her alleged role when Trump was briefed; he never got a defensive briefing, often given to U.S. citizens targeted by spies.

  • Megaspeed, already under U.S. probe for steering Nvidia chips to China, bought at least $4.8B in Nvidia gear via a sister firm, and remains an Nvidia cloud partner.

  • Nvidia called Jensen’s meetings with Ms. Huang routine, saying customers get ordinary business info and “zero information relevant to national security.”

  • Megaspeed said outside counsel is investigating and it’s cooperating with the U.S., while China called the claims “groundless smears and slanders.”

Why it matters: The report reads like a spy thriller, but nothing has been publicly proven, including whether Ms. Huang passed anything to China. The immediate fallout may hit the loophole allowing firms like Megaspeed to rent Nvidia-powered computing from Southeast Asia to Chinese AI labs — one Trump reopened but may now close.

TOGETHER WITH OPENART

🧑‍🎨 Create a launch video for your business 

The Rundown: Need a launch video for your business? Simply paste your website link, add your brand assets, and define your target audience. OpenArt’s AI video agent will shape the story and messaging while handling the script, motion design, voiceover, and video editing.

With OpenArt, you can:

  • Turn your website, screenshots, or pitch deck into a launch video

  • Create short promos or longer videos to showcase your business

  • Refine scenes, voiceovers, or music by describing the changes

  • Go beyond launches with product ads and UGC-style videos

Create your launch video with OpenArt.

ROWAN’S CORNER

🤖 ‘Sent from my agent’

h/t to @gregisenberg for the tweet

Rowan: “Sent from my agent” is becoming the new “Sent from iPhone.” That’s a tweet my friend Greg Isenberg recently made that’s stirring up conversation.

Basically, “Sent from my iPhone” started as a way to buy forgiveness for typos and messy formatting when emailing someone from your iPhone. But when someone sees “Sent from my agent,” the real message they receive is: you weren’t worth my attention.

There’s real tension here (for me included). Agents are the biggest leverage available right now, and I run several tasks through them, saving me at least a few hours a week. But I also believe going the extra mile and writing something yourself shows the other human respect.

So here’s my line:

  1. Anything that touches a person is me — social posts, messages, recruiting calls, live video.

  2. Anything that’s a task, an agent can do.

I also have a growing thesis that real human relationships will only become more valuable as AI gets better. Anything that risks that trust is probably a bad trade. Personally, if I see “sent from my agent,” I’m deleting the email.

I’ve written before that AI intuition is the most important skill of this decade, knowing which tasks to hand to AI, and this is the perfect example. Use agents everywhere, except on people.

Are you using agents to respond to your emails, or do you think the human touch shows respect? Let me know in the poll at the bottom of the email. I’m curious!

AI TRAINING

🎙️ Make ElevenLabs voiceovers sound more natural

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll add Audio Tags to a short Eleven v4 voiceover, compare it with the plain version, and create a short scene with two speakers.

Step-by-step:

  1. Open ElevenLabs Text to Speech, choose one voice, and select Eleven v4. Generate the guide’s plain script and save it for comparison

  2. Paste the tagged version without changing the spoken words. Keep the same voice and settings so you can hear the difference

  3. Compare the opening, pace, and final line. If the delivery stays flat, make one cue more specific. Change one thing at a time

  4. If a tag gets read aloud, check the model and square brackets. Keep the direction short and place it before the words it should affect

  5. Open Dialogue mode, add two voices, and generate the guide’s exchange. Check the words, speakers, and timing before downloading the clips

Pro tip: Save a plain version before adding tags. A more expressive read may still sound less natural. You can find our full cheat sheet, annotated scripts, and review checklist here.

PRESENTED BY GLEAN

🚀 From data to decisions, faster

The Rundown: Business data spans across apps, warehouses, and BI platforms, while the context behind the numbers lives in documents, tickets, and conversations. Glean’s upcoming webinar helps you bring it all together, find trusted answers, and make data-driven decisions without SQL or a BI background.

In this webinar, you’ll learn how to:

  • Query business data in natural language

  • Quickly build dashboards to track key metrics

  • Connect metrics with enterprise context

Register for the webinar and put AI to work.

ANTHROPIC / AI SAFETY

🚨 Anthropic’s AI now monitors its own conversations

Image source: Anthropic

The Rundown: Anthropic introduced “self-assessment,” a technique where Claude reviews the chat after each reply and flags potential misuse, saying the system has been active since June and catching large-scale abuse that might otherwise be missed.

The details:

  • Claude gives each conversation a quick safety verdict (whether it’s harmful, what kind of harm, and how urgent), which helps prioritize cases for human review.

  • On Claude Fable 5, it catches 78% of potentially harmful conversations flagged by a stronger classifier, and 94% of high-priority ones, at a 1% false-positive rate.

  • It helped uncover 100K+ child-abuse flags from a single API customer, reported to authorities, plus an automated romance-scam operation run through Claude Code.

  • Anthropic admits it’s weak as a lone blocker, cutting attack success in red-team tests only from 79% to 54%, though it made each successful attack cost ~4x more.

Why it matters: After Anthropic’s own reports showed Claude being misused for cyberattacks and weapons work, letting the AI check and flag misuse in its own chats is a welcome layer. Claude brings everything it understands to each judgment, but it can also share the same blind spots, meaning the system isn’t foolproof (yet!).

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Michael used Claude Cowork to build a 3D home design app

Today’s workflow comes from reader Michael Saif:

“I built this web app for a friend who is building a house. It lets you see the finished version of every room in the planned home before anything is built. I described the idea to Claude Cowork, had a short back-and-forth answering its questions, and it built the app in four stages. You can upload one or more floor plans, select a room, and view it from several rotatable 3D angles.

You can then describe how you want the room to look when completed, such as ‘Show me with a dark-colored wood floor with blue walls,’ and ask for changes, like light-colored wood floors. You can also add furniture to see how the room will look when finished, save multiple designs for each room, and export any image as a PNG. The whole build took less than an hour from start to finish.”
